newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says food self-sufficiency rate drops.
newsitem.headline: Japan says food self-sufficiency rate drops.

text.p: Japan's Agriculture Ministry said on Friday that the country's food self-sufficiency rate fell to 42 percent in fiscal 1995/96, from 46 percent the previous year and 79 percent in 1960/61.
This was the second lowest level since 1960, the ministry said in a statement. It attributed the rise to increased beef imports, among other factors.
The rate, which is calculated on a calorie basis, fell to 37 percent in fiscal 1993/94 when the rice harvest plunged due to the colder-than-usual weather.
The government said it aims to raise the rate to 46 percent by 2005/06.
